messages.content: Each paragraph of your response must end with the same word it started with, separate paragraphs with a newline.  Discuss how likely the predictions below are.  • Privacy will become a thing of the past. • By the early 2030s, we will be able to copy human consciousness to a computer. • Wireless Internet connection will be available anywhere on our planet. • All forms of transport will eventually become electric. • The effects of climate change will be irreversible. • Physical money (coins and notes) won't exist anymore. • Scientists will unlock the genetic secrets that could allow us to live for centuries, maybe forever.

message.content:
privacy is more likely to become thinner than extinct, since surveillance, data trade, and leaks expand exposure, while rights and cryptography preserve some personal control; privacy
consciousness copying by early 2030s is extremely unlikely because mapping memory, subjective experience, and biological function remains far beyond current science and engineering; consciousness
wireless internet coverage becoming nearly ubiquitous by 2030s is fairly likely in cities and many rural areas due to satellites and cellular networks, yet true everywhere on Earth remains harder because terrain, oceans, deserts, and policy can block access; wireless
transport becoming fully electric is possible over centuries but not certain, since batteries, fuels, infrastructure, and energy sources constrain many vehicles, especially heavy freight and aviation; transport
climate change producing irreversible impacts is already likely, with coral loss, ice-sheet collapse, and ecosystem shifts that may outlast human lifetimes even if emissions stop; climate
money in coins and notes may shrink dramatically in rich countries but likely will persist in places with low digital access or informal economies, so full disappearance is less probable; money
science unlocking genetic secrets that permit centuries or immortality remains far less likely, because aging involves many systems, safety is hard, and biological limits may resist even brilliant discoveries; science
